sights.name: Steiner Tor
sights.content: One of the old city gates, dating from the 15th century.

sights.name: Kunsthalle Krems
sights.hours: Summer: Tue-Sun and holidays 10:00-18:00; winter: Tue-Sun and holidays 10:00-17:00
sights.content: Hosts exhibits of art by regional as well as international artists.

sights.name: Karikatur Museum Krems
sights.content: A good knowledge of German is helpful in understanding some of the humor presented here.

sights.name: Museumkrems
sights.hours: Apr-May Wed-Sun, holidays 11:00-18:00; Jun-Oct Daily 11:00-18:00; closed Nov-Mar
sights.content: Has well-curated permanent exhibits illustrating the history of Krems and the wider region, and hosts temporary exhibits of contemporary art.

sights.name: Gozzoburg
sights.content: Built in the 13th century, this is one of the most significant medieval city buildings in Austria, and is now used for special exhibits. In 2006 and 2007 restoration work uncovered a remarkable set of 13th-century frescoes; along with the '

sights.name: Jewish Cemetery Krems
sights.content: Established in 1880 for the Jewish community of Krems, the cemetery was abandoned in 1936 and now is a memorial under the auspices of Vienna Israelite Community. Located on the grounds is a 42m-long metal memorial by Hans Kupelwieser, engra

sights.name: Piaristenkirche
sights.content: The oldest church in Krems. The earliest foundations date to the 13th century, while the current structure is from the late Gothic period of the early 16th century. The interior was remodeled during the Baroque era.

sights.name: Burgruine Rehberg
sights.hours: Outer castle open 24 hrs, inner castle by prior arrangement only
sights.content: Established in the 12th century, the castle changed hands many times over the centuries before it was finally abandoned in the early 19th century.

sights.name: Burgruine Senftenberg
sights.content: The castle is located few kilometers north of Krems. Built in the 12th century, the fortress was abandoned after the Thirty Years' War. Easily accessible by foot and offers a great view of the surrounding vineyards.

foodDrink.name: Filmbar im Kesselhaus
foodDrink.content: The student restaurant-bar is located by the cinema, and serves some vegetarian dishes along with regional classics. Reservations can be made by telephone or by email.

foodDrink.name: Schwarze Kuchl
foodDrink.content: Serves traditional regional cuisine, including some vegetarian dishes.

foodDrink.name: Piano – das Bierlokal
foodDrink.content: Offers beer from Austria, Germany and Czech Republic with a focus on beer from the nearby Waldviertel.

foodDrink.name: Winzer Krems
foodDrink.hours: Wine shop: Mon-Fri 08:00-17:00, Sat 10:00-17:00, May-Oct also on Sun and holidays 10:00-16:00

foodDrink.name: Shopping Center Eisenstadt
foodDrink.content: Grocery market, clothes, cosmetics, hair dresser, books, travel agency.

foodDrink.name: FMZ Haidäcker Park
foodDrink.content: Cosmetics, grocery market, books, sports, glasses, shoes.

foodDrink.name: FMZ Rusterstraße
foodDrink.content: Cosmetics, sports, animals, books, school, shoes.

sights.name: Bratislava Castle
sights.content: The castle contains a Museum of Bratislava History, and a baroque garden. There is also a restaurant open till after the actual castle tours into the night. The general precinct area immediately outside the castle, including the vantage poi

sights.name: Slovak National Gallery (SNG)
sights.content: For a taste of '''visual arts''', pay a visit to the National Gallery at the embankment between Starý most and Nový most with permanent collections of Slovak and European medieval art pieces, although the temporary exhibitions tend to be fa

sights.name: Bratislava City Gallery (GMB)
sights.content: Bratislava City Gallery is also a good pick to see displays of historical fine arts, paintings and sculptures along with interesting temporary exhibitions.

sights.name: Danubiana Meulensteen Art Museum
sights.content: If you like modern art better, pay a visit to the Danubiana Art Museum on the southern edge of Bratislava. It is about 20km from the city center, so too far to walk. Take bus nr 90 from the National Theater, a taxi, or drive. It is located

sights.name: National Museum
sights.content: Permanent archaelogical collections.

sights.name: Natural Science Museum
sights.content: Echoing the communist era, the natural science exhibitions have an interesting collection of artifacts and is slowly being transformed into a modern era exhibition.

sights.name: Gerulata
sights.content: This is an ancient Roman military camp with archeological findings on display. If you're into all things Roman, you should also consider a visit to the nearby '''[http://www.carnuntum.at/de Carnuntum]''' which has a large archeological site

sights.name: Museum of Transport
sights.price: Adults €8, students and seniors 65-70 €4, children 3-6 and seniors 70+ €1, children under 3 free. Free entry on first Wednesday of each month
sights.content: With a display of historical vehicles (automobiles, farm vehicles, bicycles, firefighting vehicles, railway, model ships and model buses) in the first railway station in the city, very close to the current Main Railway Station. Free parking

sights.name: Museum of City History
sights.content: Including the museums of history and music as well as the city dungeon and the exhibition on medieval justice.

sights.name: Devín Castle
sights.price: €8 April to October, €6 November to March
sights.content: There has been a fortress on this site since Roman times. In the 19th and early 20th century it became a Slovak national symbol. During the Communist dictatorship, it was part of the border zone which prevented people from escaping the coun

sights.name: St. Martin's Cathedral
sights.content: The largest and one of the oldest churches in Bratislava, situated below Bratislava Castle. The Gothic cathedral, formerly the coronation-church of several Hungarian kings, begun in 1204, and reconsecrated in 1445, was restored in 1861-80.

sights.name: Church of St. Elisabeth
sights.content: Nicknamed the '''Blue Church''' (Modrý kostolík), this is a beautiful Jugendstil church finished in 1913.

sights.name: Primate's Palace
sights.content: Now the seat of the Mayor of Bratislava.

sights.name: Old Town Hall
sights.content: The Old Town Hall and Apponyi Palace is open to the public as a museum, with an exhibition of city history.

sights.name: Grassalkovich Palace and gardens
sights.content: Also known as the '''Presidential Palace''' (Prezidentský palác) - a Rococo/late Baroque summer palace with a French garden, used as a seat of the President of Slovakia. In one of the garden's alleys you will see a row of trees planted by f

sights.name: Gallery Nedbalka
sights.content: Gallery of modern Slovak art from the late 19th century, in a building reminiscent of the New York Guggenheim.

sights.name: Mirbach Palace
sights.content: Rococo Palace built 1768–1770. Today it hosts the Bratislava City Gallery.

sights.name: Palffy Palace
sights.content: Rebuilt in the classical style in the 19th century by Count John Pálffy. Part of the Bratislava City Gallery.

sights.name: Slovak Radio Building
sights.content: Its main building is a peculiar 60-m-high reversed pyramid from the communist era and a landmark in sharp contrast with the building of the Slovak National Bank just across the street.

sights.name: Slavín monument
sights.content: On the top of the hill behind the castle, overlooking the entire city. This is a monument in memory of Soviet casualties in the liberation battle of Bratislava in World War II. It is the highest place in the city, and thus the best place fo

sights.name: Roland Fountain
sights.content: Built by stone cutter Andreas Luttringer and commissioned by Hungarian king Maximilian in 1527, this was the first fountain in Bratislava.

sights.name: Michael's Gate with Tower
sights.content: This 51-m-high tower above the gate with its green copper roof is one of the best known and the oldest buildings in Bratislava. It was built in the 14th century as one of the four gates to the city.

sights.name: SNP Bridge
sights.price: Entrance €6.50, but is free of charge if you eat in the restaurant
sights.content: A bridge over the Danube river, with its flying saucer-shaped structure housing a restaurant called [http://bratislava-slovakia.eu/places/sightseeing/ufo-tower "UFO"]. There is an observation deck on its roof, open from 10:00-23:00 daily, o

foodDrink.name: Góvinda reštaurácia
foodDrink.content: Hare Krishna-operated restaurant popular with vegans and very affordable.

foodDrink.name: KGB Krčma Gurmánov Bratislavy
foodDrink.content: Communism-themed pub with high-quality beers and affordable prices.

foodDrink.name: U Sedliaka
foodDrink.content: Good typical Slovak dishes and great background music. Nice atmosphere at affordable price.

foodDrink.name: Divný Janko Reštaurácia
foodDrink.content: Slovak and international dishes in a nice, retro ambience, the only downside is that the staff can be rude.

foodDrink.name: Slovak Pub
foodDrink.content: For good and reasonably priced halušky, the unique Slovak national meal, visit the Slovak Pub on Obchodna. This is a traditional eatery with a nice ambience. Portion size leans towards the small side. Not wheelchair accessible.

foodDrink.name: Flagship
foodDrink.content: Slovak national cuisine including halušky, in a converted theatre. Lacklustre service. Same company as Slovak Pub, who also own brewery Kláštorný pivovar, and café Franz Xaver Messerschmidt next door.

foodDrink.name: San Marten
foodDrink.content: San Marten is an Italian restaurant with great food and excellent service at affordable prices.

foodDrink.name: Mille Baci
foodDrink.content: Italian restaurant specializing in dishes from Veneto.

foodDrink.name: UFO
foodDrink.content: You can get a nice view and can meet some local celebrities at the übercool and very expensive UFO restaurant and disco on top of Nový most bridge.

foodDrink.name: ECK
foodDrink.content: Regarded as one of the best restaurants in Slovakia, bookings open two months in advance and sell out almost immediately.

cityEats.name: the guest house
cityEats.hours: Mo-Su 06:30-24:00; PH open "365 Tage im Jahr offen "

cityEats.name: Cafe - Restaurant im Otto Wagner Pavillon

guideSights.name: Stephansdom
guideSights.note: Yet another patchwork of architectural styles, but predominantly Gothic. None of the original construction remains, the oldest extant sections are the thirteenth century Giant Gate (''Riesentor'') and Towers of the Heathens (''Heidentürme''

guideSights.name: Kaisergruft
guideSights.note: Underneath the Kapuzinerkirche, this mausoleum houses the tombs of generations of Habsburg royalty.

guideSights.name: Jesuitenkirche
guideSights.note: Has one of the most elaborate Baroque interiors in Europe.

guideSights.name: Ruprechtskirche
guideSights.note: Believed to be the oldest church in Vienna, although excavations around the foundations of two other churches (Stephansdom and Peterskirche) have challenged this view. Earliest mention of the church in historical records is in 1200; the cur

guideSights.name: Peterskirche
guideSights.note: The church is believed to date back to the Middle Ages, and excavations suggest that the foundation may be far older than previously believed. The current structure was built during the Baroque period, and restored from 1998-2004 to return

guideSights.name: Maria am Gestade
guideSights.note: This gothic church was used by sailors on the Danube river. Its name refers to the former location near the river. Communion celebrations are held in German, French, and Czech.

guideSights.name: Kaiserappartements
guideSights.note: This trio of museums includes the '''Imperial Apartments''' (''Kaiserappartements''), '''Sisi Museum''', and '''Imperial Silver Collection''' (''Silberkammer''). The Imperial Apartments and Sisi Museum include 22 state rooms of the resident

guideSights.name: Schatzkammer
guideSights.note: The best part of the Hofburg and an absolute must. It contains the Habsburgs' collection of jewels, crowns, and other valuables, perhaps the best on the Continent. Second only to a tour of the Kunsthistorisches Museum, of which the Schatzka

guideSights.name: New Palace
guideSights.note: The newest and largest section of the Imperial Palace. It contains the Welt Museum Wien, the Papyrus Museum, and three branches of the Museum of Fine Arts.

guideSights.name: The House of Austrian History
guideSights.note: The House of Austrian History is a modern museum located in the Hofburg complex that explores Austria’s history from the late 19th century to the present. Through multimedia exhibits and historical artefacts, it focuses on key events such a

guideSights.name: Prunksaal
guideSights.note: This magnificent historic library was designed by Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach and built in 1726. As well as the spectacular room itself, you can see temporary exhibitions on various historical subjects.

guideSights.name: Globenmuseum
guideSights.note: The only museum of its type in the world, this museum contains a collection of 650 globes of all types, as well as a collection of nearly 300,000 historic maps.

guideSights.name: Esperantomuseum
guideSights.note: Founded in 1927, this museum houses a library and museum with displays illustrating the development and grammar of the modern invented language Esperanto.

guideSights.name: Albertina
guideSights.note: Once a palace, it is now the most popular exhibition space in Vienna, mainly for traditional modern art. The building itself is an experience as well. It is home to a valuable drawing collection, including many works of the German Renaissan

guideSights.name: Herzgruft, Augustinerkirche
guideSights.note: Yet another example of the gruesome divide-and-conquer burial strategy of the Habsburg dynasty. It is said that other dynasties waged countless wars to acquire new lands, but "you, happy Austria, marry". Even in death, the Habsburgs placate

guideSights.name: Hofburgkapelle
guideSights.note: The original chapel of the Palace, built in Gothic style 1447-1449, was made over in Baroque style. On Sundays and Catholic holidays (of which the Austrians celebrate many), the Court Musicians perform here. This group is made up of members

guideSights.name: Spanish Riding School
guideSights.note: First mentioned in a document dated 1572, it is the only equestrian institute in the world which follows a Renaissance model of classical schooling. Eleves, or students, begin their training immediately after completion of Austrian primary

guideSights.name: Schmetterlinghaus
guideSights.note: A tropical greenhouse with an amazing collection of live butterflies, will delight both children and adults.

guideSights.name: Kunsthistorisches Museum
guideSights.note: One of the world's greatest art museums and in a palace that is a work of art itself. Serious art fans may wish to devote more than a day to its treasures. There is no other word to describe the ''Kunst'' other than mind-boggling. It contai

guideSights.name: Naturhistorisches Museum
guideSights.note: This museum was erected as a mirror to its twin museum, the Museum of Fine Arts. It exhibits various minerals, meteorites, fossils, stuffed animals, and skeleton reconstructions of dinosaurs and other. It also includes an anthropological se

guideSights.name: Winterpalais des Prinzen Eugen
guideSights.note: This Baroque palace was built as a residence for Prince Eugene of Savoy, and later used for the Court Treasury and Ministry of Finance. It now houses period furnishings and exhibits detailing the biography of the prince and the history of t

guideSights.name: MAK
guideSights.note: The museum has the MAK Design Shop and a study collection. The museum emphasises design and decorative arts, and has a huge furniture collection. Early 20th century, especially Vienna Secession, and modern design are very well represented,

guideSights.name: Haus der Musik
guideSights.note: This is a relatively new and special museum devoted to an interactive learning experience. It covers the history of the Vienne Philharmonic Orchestra, the history of Vienna as a centre of music making (Mozart, Haydn, Beethoven, Mahler, Schu

guideSights.name: Museum am Schottenstift
guideSights.note: A nice, small picture gallery mainly of Baroque Austrian painting.

guideSights.name: Gemäldegalerie der Akademie der bildenden Künste
guideSights.note: A gallery owned by the Academy of Fine Arts, to which Hitler applied to before he decided to change to politics. It offers some paintings by Rubens and Bosch. Most interesting are the Renaissance and medieval exponents.

guideSights.name: Museum Postsparkasse
guideSights.note: SIGNA, the owner of the Post Office Savings Bank building, runs the WAGNER:WERK Museum Postsparkasse. Opened by BAWAG P.S.K. in 2005, it's in the small banking hall. The museum and the main banking hall are open to visitors. At the post off

guideSights.name: Österreichisches Filmmuseum
guideSights.note: A cinema for showing specially curated films and retrospective.

guideSights.name: Uhrenmuseum
guideSights.note: A collection of 3000 clocks of all types, including a prized 18th-century astronomical clock.

guideSights.name: Bank Austria Kunstforum
guideSights.note: This venue hosts special exhibits of internationally-renowned artists; past exhibits have displayed work by Egon Schiele, Oskar Kokoschka, Cézanne, Picasso, and Van Gogh.

guideSights.name: Phantastenmuseum
guideSights.note: An unusual museum dedicated to the work of the Vienna School of Fantastic Realism (''Wiener Schule des Phantastischen Realismus''), highlighting works by artists Ernst Fuchs, Arik Brauer, Rudolf Hausner, Wolfgang Hutter and Fritz Janschka.

guideSights.name: Dommuseum
guideSights.note: A collection of liturgical implements, illustrated manuscripts, altarpieces, and sculptures.

guideSights.name: Österreichisches Theatermuseum
guideSights.note: Housed in the Baroque Lobkowitz Palace, this museum displays stage models, costumes, and props, with special temporary exhibits.

guideSights.name: MUSA Museum Startgalerie Artothek
guideSights.note: Hosts special exhibits of contemporary Austrian art.

guideSights.name: Beethoven Pasqualatihaus
guideSights.note: This 18th-century building is atop the Mölker Bastei, one of the only remaining sections of the old city wall. For 8 years Beethoven lived in a 4th-floor apartment in this building, where he composed his 4th-8th symphonies as well as his op

guideSights.name: Jüdisches Museum Wien
guideSights.note: A museum documenting the history of Vienna's substantial Jewish community which included Zweig, Freud, Herzl, Mahler, and Schoenberg. Three sites are available for one combined ticket: two museum sites and the main synagogue. Attached to th

guideSights.name: Jüdisches Museum Judenplatz
guideSights.note: A second branch of the Jewish Museum on Dorotheergasse. Underneath the Judenplatz (the Jewish Square) is an underground medieval synagogue excavation. Amazingly, the synagogue was destroyed centuries ago, but its existence was remembered by

guideSights.name: Stadttempel
guideSights.note: A well preserved 19th-century synagogue, which is being used as the main city's synagogue by the current growing Viennese Jewish community.

guideSights.name: Ausgrabungen Michaelerplatz
guideSights.note: Archeological excavations carried out between 1989 and 1991 revealed not only the foundations of medieval buildings but also remains of the Roman canabae (civilian support settlement) of Vindobona, as Vienna was then known. The viewing area

guideSights.name: Mozarthaus Vienna
guideSights.note: This is the Viennese residence of Austria's most famous composer, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, and a branch of the Vienna Museum.

guideSights.name: Neidhart Fresken
guideSights.note: The oldest secular wall paintings known in Vienna, in a 14th-century building. The frescoes were commissioned in 1398 and illustrate scenes from the life and poetry of the Viennese minnesinger Neidhart von Reuental.

guideSights.name: Römermuseum
guideSights.note: This museum houses a collection of artifacts from the Roman settlement of Vindobona, as Vienna was then known. There are Roman ruins in the cellar of the museum, first discovered during construction work in 1948, and for many years only acc

guideSights.name: Römische Baureste Am Hof
guideSights.note: Early Roman ruins from Vienna's earliest days as a Roman fort in the basement of the Fire Brigade Building.

guideSights.name: Virgilkapelle
guideSights.note: A 13th-century subterranean chapel beneath the former Chapel of St Mary Magdalene (no longer standing, but outlines have been traced on the pavement directly south of Stephansdom). This chapel served as the tomb for a wealthy Viennese famil

guideSights.name: Heldenplatz
guideSights.note: A public space in front of the Neue Hofburg, setting to a number of important historic events, most notably of Adolf Hitler's 1938 announcement of the Austrian Anschluß. Two 19th-century equestrian statues portray Archduke Charles of Austri

guideSights.name: Stock im Eisen
guideSights.note: The remaining midsection of a medieval nail tree (Nagelbaum). Over the centuries hundreds of nails have been hammered in both in thanksgiving and for good luck. The tree figures in a number of local legends.

guideSights.name: Parlamentsgebäude
guideSights.note: The home of the two houses of Austrian Parliament. The building was designed by Theophil von Hansen in the Neoclassical style, and constructed between 1873 and 1883. [https://www.parlament.gv.at/ENGL/GEBF/FUEHRUNGEN/index.shtml Guided tours

guideSights.name: Wiener Secession
guideSights.note: Architect Josef Maria Olbrich built this Jugendstil (German-style Art Nouveau) building 1897-98 as a display space for artists working in the new Secession artistic movement. It is topped by a giant, frothy golden ball, lovingly called ''Kr

guideSights.name: Wiener Rathaus
guideSights.note: Designed by Friedrich von Schmidt (the architect of the Cologne Cathedral) and completed in 1883, this is the most significant neo-Gothic building in Vienna, with a 103m-high clock tower. There is a very pleasant park with two fountains in

guideSights.name: Ankeruhr
guideSights.note: A large 4-m-diameter musical clock on a pedestrian bridge connecting two neighboring buildings. The clock was designed between 1911 and 1914 by the Judgenstil painter Franz Matsch, and features prominent figures from Viennese history, each

guideSights.name: Looshaus
guideSights.note: Designed by Adolf Loos and completed in 1909, this is considered to be one of the most significant buildings of the Wiener Moderne era from 1890-1910, although initially it was fiercely criticised. Today the building is occupied by the Wien

guideSights.name: Universität Wien
guideSights.note: The university was founded in 1365, and is the oldest university in the German-speaking area, as well as one of the largest in Europe with more than 90,000 students. It consists of 15 faculties amongst them are Law, Mathematics, Physics, Ps

guideSights.name: Stadtpark
guideSights.note: Court painter Joseph Selleny and garden director Rudolf Siebeck designed this kind of artificial park with several small landscapes. It opened on the 21 August 1862. It houses the golden statue of Johann Strauss, which is most frequently ph

guideSights.name: Rathauspark
guideSights.note: The park is symmectric with a big square in the middle in front of the city hall. The park has on each grassy side a varied selection of woody plants a Japanese pagoda tree or umbrella tree and an old ginkgo.

guideSights.name: Volksgarten
guideSights.note: The park is famous for the big variation of beautiful roses and features old platanes. There is a monument for Empress Elizabeth and in the middle a neoclassical Theseus temple.

guideSights.name: Burggarten
guideSights.note: It has the form of an English garden, and is directly adjacent to the Hofburg. It has a statue of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. In the summertime students like to hang out in middle of the trees.

guideSights.name: Österreichische Galerie Belvedere
guideSights.note: Contains recent Austrian and international art from the past two centuries. Viennese art from the early 20th century is well-represented in the permanent collection ''Vienna around 1900 and the Art of the Classical Modern'', and includes ma

guideSights.name: Unteres Belvedere
guideSights.note: The Lower Belvedere and Orangery house temporary exhibits. The Baroque state rooms including the Marble Gallery, Golden Room, and Grotesque Hall are open for normal visiting.

guideSights.name: 21er Haus
guideSights.note: Has a permanent exhibit of works by the Austrian sculptor/architect Fritz Wotruba, and hosts rotating exhibits of international contemporary art.

guideSights.name: KunstHausWien
guideSights.note: Even an avowed hater of modern art can appreciate this. This is Hundertwasser's (born Friedrich Stowasser in 1928) major contribution to the Viennese art world. In a time when artists often try to shock the public or merely impress other me

guideSights.name: Heeresgeschichtliches Museum
guideSights.note: A huge museum featuring weapons and military maps from different periods. You can also see the open-top car in which Archduke Franz Ferdinand, the last Austrian prince, was shot in Sarajevo. His death triggered World War I and the eventual

guideSights.name: Remise - Verkehrsmuseum der Wiener Linien
guideSights.note: This museum in a former depot houses a comprehensive collection of vintage vehicles explaining the history of Viennese public transport. The exhibits include horse-drawn streetcars from 1868, a steam tram set from 1885, many electric street

guideSights.name: Hundertwasserhaus
guideSights.note: Interesting apartment/office complex, designed by the Austrian architect/painter Hundertwasser. Remember that most of it is still in use as housing or offices and respect the residents' privacy. The nearby KunstHausWien (see above) is a Hun

guideSights.name: Heldendenkmal der Roten Armee
guideSights.note: An imposing Soviet-style monument near Karlsplatz commemorates the Soviet victory in Vienna over the Nazi army.

guideSights.name: Arnold Schönberg Center
guideSights.note: This building houses an archive of the works of the Viennese composer, with a permanent exhibit relating to his work and music and a gallery of his paintings.

guideSights.name: Sankt Marxer Friedhof
guideSights.note: This historic cemetery was in use from 1784 until 1874. Mozart was buried here in an unmarked pauper's grave in 1791; the tombstone dates from a later period, after his grave was tentatively identified. The [http://www.bezirksmuseum.at/de/b

guideSights.name: Botanischer Garten
guideSights.note: Established in 1754 by Empress Maria Theresia as a garden for medicinal plants and granted to the University of Vienna, which has maintained it since. The gardens contain a number of rare plants, including alpine specimens.

guideSights.name: Wien Museum Karlsplatz
guideSights.note: A museum documenting Vienna's history. It is split into several branches with its main branch at Karlsplatz.

guideSights.name: Dritte Mann Museum
guideSights.note: This is a private museum dedicated to the cult film ''The Third Man'', which was shot in Vienna and released in 1949. This film is often played at the '''Burgkino'''.

guideSights.name: Generali Foundation
guideSights.note: This private foundation houses large collection of contemporary art, with a special focus on photograph, film, video, and installation pieces. The archives and library are also open to the public.

guideSights.name: Schubert Sterbewohnung
guideSights.note: The composer Franz Schubert died here in 1828. The small museum displays documents relating to the composer's life and work.

guideSights.name: Karlskirche
guideSights.note: Largest Baroque church north of the Alps, designed by the famous architect Bernhard Fischer von Erlach. Frescos done by Michael Rottmayr and paintings from the Italian Baroque painters Sebastiano Ricci and Giuseppe Antonio Pellegrini, and t

guideSights.name: Karlsplatz Stadtbahn Pavilion
guideSights.note: An original entrance building for the Wiener Stadtbahn railway station at Karlsplatz (now U-Bahn line U4), designed by Otto Wagner. It is a good example of functional turn of the century architecture – ornate, yet useful. Wagner was one of

guideSights.name: Paulanerkirche
guideSights.note: Built in the 17th century, the current appearance of the church is largely Baroque.

guideSights.name: Palais Schönburg
guideSights.note: The small Baroque garden palace is one of the earlier works of Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt. It was modified in the 19th century, and these days used as an event location.

guideSights.name: Margareten-Hof
guideSights.note: Built by the architects Ferdinand Fellner und Hermann Helmer in 1884/85.

guideSights.name: Margaretenbrunnen
guideSights.note: It was built to thank for the access to the fresh water pipeline going to the central imperial palace for Margareten in 1835/36. It features Saint Margarete killing a dragon.

guideSights.name: Matzleinsdorfer Pfarrkirche
guideSights.note: Two previous churches were located here, the most recent a Baroque building from the 18th century, which despite massive popular protest was demolished in 1965 due to traffic considerations. The new steel and concrete church was designed by

guideSights.name: Reumannhof
guideSights.note: During a short period from 1919 to 1933, the city of Vienna erected some 65,000 apartments of high quality for the impoverished working class. Highly noticeable is also the contemporary architecture of these buildings all across town, of wh

guideSights.name: Haydnhaus
guideSights.note: Joseph Haydn spent the final twelve years of his life in this home, during which time he composed the oratorios ''The Creation'' and ''The Seasons''. The house has been a museum since 1899, and careful restoration has included the small gar

guideSights.name: Haus des Meeres
guideSights.note: A marvelous zoo, with a rain forest glasshouse, tiny apes, aquariums with sharks, and terrariums with reptiles and venomous snakes. Other highlights include an interesting exhibit of Mediterranean sea life and the aquarium's beloved sea tur

guideSights.name: Rahlstiege
guideSights.note: The staircase connects the Mariahilfer and the Gumpendorfer Strasse. It was built in 1870.

guideSights.name: Leopold Museum
guideSights.note: Has a strict policy of not allowing big bags inside the museum. Even your cameras (unless they can be tucked inside a small carry bag) will have to be deposited outside.

guideSights.name: MUMOK
guideSights.note: Has a strict policy of not allowing big bags inside the museum. Even your cameras (unless they can be tucked inside a small carry bag) will have to be deposited outside. Has a self-service locker.

guideSights.name: Kunsthalle Wien
guideSights.note: Hosts highly-regarded exhibits of contemporary art, from Austrian and international artists.

guideSights.name: Möbel Museum Wien
guideSights.note: Houses the largest furniture collection in the world. The exhibit displays furniture for all the Austrian emperors since Charles VI (the father of Maria Theresa), furniture by the Thonet Brothers, Jugendstil, and the Viennese Modernist move

guideSights.name: Palais Auersperg
guideSights.note: The palace was built in the early 18th century, and expanded in the late 18th century under the ownership of Prince Adam von Auersperg. Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach drew up the first plans; later designs are attributed to Johann Lucas

guideSights.name: Palais Damian
guideSights.note: The palace changed hands frequently, with each owner making their own adaptations to the building. The central sections date from the early 18th century, while the second floor was a later addition.

guideSights.name: Palais Schönborn
guideSights.note: This impressive Baroque palace was built in 1706-1711 following the designs of Johann Lukas von Hildebrandt. It houses the '''Museum of Folk Life and Folk Art''' (''Museum für Volkskunde'') (see listing below).

guideSights.name: Palais Strozzi
guideSights.note: The palace was built in 1702, and once had a garden that extended to Pfeilgasse. Renovations in 1996 led to the rediscovery of old paintings dating to the period of the building's construction.

guideSights.name: Piarist Church
guideSights.note: The Baroque church Maria Treu was probably designed by Lukas von Hildebrandt. The church has eight chapels and is decorated with frescoes made by Franz Anton Maulbertsch. It is considered as an important religious building of its time. In 1

guideSights.name: Wiener Schuhmuseum
guideSights.note: The only museum of its kind in Austria, with displays focusing on the history of shoemaking.

guideSights.name: Österreichisches Museum für Volkskunde
guideSights.note: Founded in 1895 and housed in the Schönborn Garden Palace, this museum is dedicated to preserving the traditional folk art of Austria and of central Europe, with rotating exhibits as well as a permanent display. There is a museum library an

guideSights.name: Liechtenstein Museum
guideSights.note: A private collection of the Prince of Liechtenstein is exhibited in his former Viennese residences, which include the Stadtpalais (City Palace) and Gartenpalais (Garden Palace). The richly decorated picture gallery mainly exhibits Baroque p

guideSights.name: Pathologisch-anatomisches Bundesmuseum
guideSights.note: Housed in a squat tower, which once was an insane asylum, the Narrenturm (''Fool's Tower''), this museum contains some of the dustier corners of the annals of medicine. You will find preserved hydrocephalic infants, wax castings of tertiary

guideSights.name: Josephinum
guideSights.note: Founded by Emperor Joseph II as the Academy of Medico-Surgery, the building was completed in 1785 and houses nearly 1200 anatomical wax models commissioned by the emperor, along with medical documents and instruments. The Josephinum is stil

guideSights.name: Votivkirche
guideSights.note: One of the most important Neo-Gothic religious architectural sites in the world, constructed between 1856 and 1879. Stands on a large square on the location where an unsuccessful attempt to assassinate Emperor Franz Joseph took place in 185

guideSights.name: Spittelau Waste Incineration Plant
guideSights.note: A waste incinerator may not be the usual item to attract a visitor's attention, but after the Viennese painter/architect Friedensreich Hundertwasser restyled the plant's façade in 1989 (following a fire in 1987), it has become a surprisingl

guideSights.name: Strudlhofstiege
guideSights.note: Designed by Theodor Johann Jaeger and completed in 1910, the outdoor staircase connects Strudlhofgasse and Liechtensteinstraße, and is a significant example of Jugendstil architecture.

guideSights.name: St. Johannes Nepomuk Kapelle
guideSights.note: Designed by Otto Wagner between 1893 bis 1897, this is the architect's first religious structure and served as a model for his later ''Kirche am Steinhof''.

guideSights.name: Freud Museum
guideSights.note: This small museum is in Freud's historic flat where he practiced psychoanalysis for almost his whole life. However, the collection is limited mostly to documents of various kinds relating to Freud's life. Almost all of the flat's contents,

guideSights.name: Schubert Geburtshaus
guideSights.note: Franz Schubert was born in a small apartment in this house in 1797. The museum, just like the apartment itself, is rather small and not wheelchair accessible. The top floor displays documents relating to the composer's life and work, while

guideSights.name: Jüdischer Friedhof Seegasse
guideSights.note: Vienna's oldest preserved Jewish cemetery, in use from the 16th century until 1784. In 1941 Nazi officials decided to raze the cemetery; in response a number of Viennese Jews removed 931 gravestones and buried them at the Zentralfriedhof. I

guideSights.name: Wurstelprater
guideSights.note: This year-round amusement park (map available [https://www.wien.gv.at/umwelt/parks/anlagen/images/pratertafel.jpg here] was established in the late 18th century, and is most famous for its '''Riesenrad''' (see listing below). The park also

guideSights.name: Riesenrad
guideSights.note: An English engineering firm (Walter Basset) built the giant Ferris wheel from 1896-97. Others of the same era, built for world exhibitions and other parks in Chicago, London, Paris, etc. have long since been torn down. The Riesenrad has bec

guideSights.name: Zeiss Planetarium Wien
guideSights.note: Offers a variety of shows, and guided tours.

guideSights.name: Pratermuseum
guideSights.note: A small museum devoted to the history of popular entertainment.

guideSights.name: Johann Strauß Wohnung
guideSights.note: The 'Waltz King' lived in this elegant apartment from 1863 until 1870; his most famous piece 'An der schönen blauen Donau' (The Blue Danube) was composed during his time here. Included with the items on display is one of the composer's viol

guideSights.name: Wiener Kriminalmuseum
guideSights.note: This museum is dedicated to the history of police and the justice system, from the Middle Ages until World War II. Exhibits relating to famous Viennese criminals are included.

guideSights.name: Circus- und Clownmuseum
guideSights.note: This unusual museum houses a collection of props and costumes, with rotating exhibits.

guideSights.name: Thyssen-Bronemisza Art Comtemporary
guideSights.note: The venue formerly known as Augarten Contemporary is now operated by the TBA21 Foundation, under contract with the Belvedere Museum. The building hosts special exhibits of contemporary art by Austrian and international artists, and has a pe

guideSights.name: Otto Wagner Schützenhaus
guideSights.note: Designed by Otto Wagner, and built in 1908, this was part of a planned redevelopment of the Donaukanal. After many years of neglect the building was fully restored in 2010, and now houses a restaurant.

guideSights.name: Flaktürme VII
guideSights.note: This is a pair of anti-aircraft defense towers/bunkers, built by the Luftwaffe during World War II. During construction multiple rail tracks were laid across the park, and it is believed that hundreds of war victims were buried in mass grav

guideSights.name: Millennium Tower
guideSights.note: At 171 metres (561 feet), the tower was Vienna's the tallest building until the DC Tower was completed across the Danube, and continues to be a poignant landmark of the district. It was designed by the architects Gustav Peichl, Boris Podrec

guideSights.name: Meldemannstraße Dormitory
guideSights.note: This was public dormitory for men (''Männerwohnheim'') from 1905 to 2003. It is of interest as it was the residence of Adolf Hitler, the Nazi German dictator from 1910 to 1913 before he moved on to Munich.

guideSights.name: Bezirksmuseum Brigittenau
guideSights.note: This little museum tells the story of the district itself through pictures, views and models.

guideSights.name: Brigittakirche
guideSights.note: This Neogothic church is a landmark of the Brigittenau district. It was built between 1868 and 1874.

guideSights.name: New Campus of the Vienna University of Economics and Business
guideSights.note: This stunning new campus opened in 2013, with buildings designed by international architecture firms from Spain, the UK, Germany, Japan, and Austria. The star of the campus is the''Library & Learning Center'', designed by British-Iraqi arch

guideSights.name: Atominstitut
guideSights.note: The 250 kW TRIGA Mark II reactor in the Viennese Prater started operation in 1962. The reactor is a training ground for International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) inspectors and neighbouring countries. The Atominstitut offers guided tours fo

guideSights.name: Technisches Museum Wien
guideSights.note: This museum exhibits machines, transportations, electronic equipment, and the like from their first design up to their current form. The museum is huge at 22,000 m² and requires at least two hours to go through.

guideSights.name: Kirche am Steinhof
guideSights.note: Opened in 1907 as part of the largest mental hospital and sanatorium of its time in Europe, this Art Nouveau church was constructed by the Viennese master architect Otto Wagner, and is the most well-known example of Jugendstil sacral archit

guideSights.name: Karl Marx-Hof
guideSights.note: Built between 1927 and 1930 by the Otto Wagner's student Karl Ehn, the Karl Marx-Hof is a public housing complex (called "Gemeindebau" in Vienna), from the time of the social-democratic public housing programme during Austria's First Republ

guideSights.name: Beethoven Wohnung Heiligenstadt
guideSights.note: One of Beethoven's many residences within the city. While living here he composed his Symphony No. 2 in D major (Op. 36), as well as several other works.

guideSights.name: Türkenschanzpark
guideSights.note: A lovely park, inaugurated in 1888 by Austrian emperor Franz Joseph. The park is at the site of and named after a Turkish entrenchment ("Türken-Schanze") of the first Turkish siege on Vienna in 1529. It is close to the University of Agricul

guideSights.name: St. Leopoldskirche
guideSights.note: Dedicated to the patron saint of Vienna, this small church was established in 1679, and its current appearance dates to the first part of the 18th century. The building is on top of 425-m-high Leopoldsberg, with lovely views of Vienna and t

guideSights.name: Grinzing Parish Church
